how: The room calls members to maintain an existing flag and later to enlarge it, rather than documenting a start from blank space.
A call for more repairers identifies insufficient hands without establishing that the whole room considers further defence impossible.
A request for help receives a bare promise to come and then a short expression of thanks.
The written request and bare acceptance support the proposed reply pattern without establishing obligations for silent readers or the treatment of refusals.
A member proposes lettering and draws instructions that others accept and begin executing.
The starter's proposal already invites collective work, leaving a distinct later call caused by that start unestablished.
The lettering proposal receives agreement followed by reported completion of the first letter.
Members debate retaining the shield, explain its pixelated appearance, and propose national symbols and Caribbean unity designs.
Builders report the R, the E and the border as successive parts of the shared lettering work.
Coordinates and drawn instructions make the flag and its additions locatable for multiple placers.
A circulated template may remain an unaccepted proposal, so publication alone cannot establish that design discussion has settled.
Members circulate a flag script, explain its console use, ask about compatibility and share a target covering both flags.
Before treating a negotiated move as executable, running targets must be checked because an absent operator cannot stop an old-location script.
Visible coordination proceeds through voluntary lettering handoffs and location questions, while decisions outside the supplied discussion and the cross-room frequency remain untestable.
Members repair stolen pixels, use three accounts, return every five minutes and direct one another toward specific damaged corners.
The heart flag claimed as made by siblings is later reported damaged and explicitly maintained by another participant.
Participants connect attacks to calls for scripts and bots, while a destruction warning receives a report of repairs through three accounts.
Escalation to scripts depends on repair scale because a few people can keep the small heart flag intact without automation.
Attribution distinguishes suspected bots, programmed attacks and the helper's own mistakes, while remaining participant explanation rather than verified identification.
A doubtful screenshot receives an admission of mistaken repair, making indirect correction visible while leaving the inaccessible image's contents unresolved.
Requests for help receive promises and thanks, while participants share scripts and report repair work benefiting both flags without a documented bargain.
A request naming the threatened neighbouring flag receives an immediate offer of a script to help defend it.
One script serving both flags and explicit solidarity instantiate informal joint defence, accompanied by proposals for visible unity.
Joint defence and unity proposals warrant an informal coalition reading but do not establish a shared hub, binding pact or completed joint square.
Shared threat and combined maintenance are visible, but the record does not isolate a separate coalition-founding event caused by the threat.
A revised plan explicitly spares the gameboy without citing a negotiated border or agreement.
The recorded restraint cites avoiding erasure rather than an established border, leaving the proposed deal-to-restraint mechanism untested.
Participants seek support for a proposal in the stronger neighbour's diplomatic thread and coordinate overlapping requests.
A member carries a proposal between the neighbour's diplomatic venue and the home discussion, where another negotiator asks whether to edit an earlier request.
An outward request supports seeking a host's permission, but conditional wording leaves approval and an operating host-guest arrangement unresolved.
The negotiation exchange explicitly invokes the old spot's loss as a reason to revise the request, without establishing a successful deal.
Help requests and replies do not cite the later diplomatic proposal as their source, and no completed border bargain establishes the proposed mechanism.
Participants weigh rebuilding at a new location against continuing to fight for the lost spot, while a separate builder announces another start.
A unified stop-fighting-then-move sequence requires cessation at the old target, whereas this room combines continued script placement, resistance to surrender and competing starts.
An after-close present-tense flag title cannot establish renewed placement or a completed move after the common placement deadline.
Editing requests and resisting relocation concern the proposed action, without an explicit challenge to who can commit the room.
No completed agreement or challenge to a negotiator's representative authority establishes the tentative transition.
Brotherhood, friendship and belonging to both countries give assistance a stated collective meaning beyond simply drawing a flag.
Complaints identify contemporary attacks but do not establish a specific quarrel inherited from before the canvas.
Historical framing and a proposed overwrite appear in separate turns without establishing that a prior tie selected the attack target.
The coded calls concern maintaining and repairing flags and provide no evidence of a host prank framing.
Visible location coordination does not establish a host rule, dedicated venue requirement or objection to canvas flooding.
Calls and coordination are visible without a recorded response drawing a boundary around canvas talk, leaving moderation elsewhere unresolved.
Progress, the heart flag, sibling authorship, smallness and final survival all become occasions for celebration and credit.
A reported contribution to the E and border receives explicit celebration of progress rather than waiting for the entire work's completion.
Participants report invisibility and erasure, while the final survival claim supplies a later account without independently verifying the final canvas.
Pride and fate reports occur without a passage establishing that celebration caused an effort to preserve the work.
A wish for more participants supports future capacity talk but leaves an actual successor effort, lasting alliance or repurposed venue unresolved.
A single title combining survival and a wish for more participants cannot establish that recording the work caused continuation.
The thin after-close titles neither expose a preserved version nor discuss cleanup, leaving any contest over preservation unresolved.
Proposals call for drawing over a Dutch crest and enlarging the flag at the gameboy's expense, without proving that either overwrite occurred.
Members denounce named attackers and curse imperialists, while the isolated anthem invocation cannot establish the speaker's allegiance or a reciprocal taunt exchange.
A building call and later overwrite proposals coexist without a passage showing that mobilisation caused participants to turn toward attack.
No refusal answering the overwrite proposals is supplied, and the earlier decision to spare the gameboy cannot serve as a later response.
No supplied answer invokes a truce or offers a deal in response to the proposed overwrites.
Contest talk already names attackers before the room's overwrite proposals, so initiating an attack cannot explain the onset of all local hostility.
